title: Represented but misread: Post-training changes how language models read out what they represent
abstract: arXiv:2611.26584v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Does post-training change what a language model represents, or how this representation is read out into an answer? We compared linear probes with the models' own answers, analyzed with signal detection theory, in six open-weight base models and their post-trained versions. For judgments of whether German texts were written by a human or an AI, probes and word n-gram classifiers separated the classes well, but the answers did not and often ordered the texts inversely. Post-training lowered the sensitivity of the answers on average ($\Delta d' = -0.34$ across model families; -0.29 across three prompts). It also changed the use of a stated base rate: Base models shifted their log-odds by less than the stated change in prior odds, most post-trained models by more. translated_title: 有所表征却被误读：后训练改变了语言模型读取其内部表征的方式
translated_abstract: 后训练究竟改变了语言模型所表征的内容，还是改变了将表征读取为答案的方式？我们在六个开源权重的基础模型及其后训练版本上，将线性探针与模型自身的回答进行了比较，并采用信号检测理论进行分析。在判断德语文本由人类还是AI撰写的任务中，线性探针和词n-gram分类器都能很好地区分类别，但模型的回答却不能，而且常常以相反的顺序排列文本。后训练平均降低了回答的灵敏度（跨模型家族Δd' = -0.34；跨三个提示词为-0.29）。它还改变了对所陈述基础比率的利用：基础模型对数几率的变化小于所陈述的先验几率变化，而大多数后训练模型的变化则更大。在两个具有阶段性检查点的模型中，这一变化发生在监督微调阶段；模型拼接实验表明相关机制位于早期层，且从中间深度开始，内部状态……（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 研究发现后训练并未破坏语言模型内部的表征（线性探针仍能准确区分人类与AI文本），而是改变了模型将表征读取为答案的方式，导致回答灵敏度下降和对先验信息的错误利用。
en_tdlr: Post-training does not corrupt what language models internally represent—linear probes still separate the classes well—but rather alters how those representations are read out into answers, degrading answer sensitivity and distorting the use of stated base rates.
